title: Distilling the Knowledge in a Neural Network
focus: Explain softmax with a temperature T applied to a small vector of logits. Let the learner edit the logits and change T. Show the scaled logits, the exponentials and the resulting probabilities. Compare a low temperature (nearly one-hot) with a high temperature (nearly uniform). Check that the probabilities always sum to one, that equal logits give equal probabilities for any T, and that the largest logit keeps the largest probability.
excerpt: Classifiers usually turn the logit z_i of each class into a probability q_i with a softmax that first divides every logit by a temperature T: q_i = exp(z_i / T) / sum_j exp(z_j / T). The ordinary softmax is the case T = 1. Raising T makes the distribution over classes softer, so classes that were given very small probabilities become visible. In the limit of very high temperature all classes approach the same probability, while a very low temperature puts almost all of the probability on the class with the largest logit. Distillation trains a small model on these softened targets produced by a large model at a high temperature.
